title: Physical Fitness & Recreation
subtitle: Five components, five tests — and why rest is in the plan.
objectives: Name the five components of health-related fitness
Name a test for each component
Explain the difference between strength and endurance
Explain why recreation is part of fitness

cards.title: Fitness is five things, not one
cards.text: "Fit" is not a single number. It is five separate abilities, and you can be strong in one and weak in the next.

cards.title: Five components, five tests
cards.text: Each one is measured differently, because each one is a different ability.
points: **Heart endurance** — a timed run or a step test.
**Muscular strength** — one maximum effort.
**Muscular endurance** — the same effort, repeated.
**Flexibility** — sit-and-reach. **Body composition** — one number of five.

cards.title: Six buttons
cards.text: Tap each component. The second line is how it is tested.

question.explain: How far a joint can move safely.

cards.title: Strength against endurance
cards.text: They are different abilities and need different training.
points: **Strength:** how much force, once.
**Endurance:** how many times you can repeat it.
**A heavy single lift** trains the first.
**Push-ups to failure** trains the second.

question.explain: Repeating the effort, not producing it once.

cards.title: Five more, for sport
cards.text: These sit beside the health five rather than replacing them.
points: **Agility, balance, coordination.**
**Power** — force produced fast.
**Reaction time** — how quickly you start.
**Health five keep you well. Skill five make you good.**

cards.title: A boxer needs all ten
cards.text: Which is why boxing training looks like five different sports.
points: **Rounds** — heart endurance.
**The clinch** — strength.
**Holding guard for twelve rounds** — muscular endurance.
**Slipping a punch** — reaction time and agility.

cards.title: Your numbers will move on their own
cards.text: At your age some of this improves without any training at all.
points: **Growth changes your leverage** and your reach.
**A test score can rise** because you got taller.
**Compare to yourself last term**, not to a classmate.
**Body composition is one of five.** It is not a verdict.

cards.title: Recreation is not the opposite of fitness
cards.text: Rest and play are part of the programme, not a break from it.
points: **Training every day without rest** makes you slower.
**Recreation keeps you doing it** for years.
**A programme you quit** beats nothing by nothing.
**Consistency is the only variable** that always matters.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Five health components, each with its own test.
Strength is one effort; endurance is many.
Skill-related fitness adds agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction.
Rest and recreation are part of the programme.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 9 MAPEH, PE strand. The week insists that fitness is five separate abilities with five separate tests, because 'fit' as a single word hides the one distinction the paper always asks about: strength against muscular endurance. Skill-related fitness is introduced beside the health five rather than instead of them. Two cards do pastoral work that matters at this age: scores move with growth, so the comparison is to his own earlier self, and body composition is one number out of five rather than a verdict. Recreation is argued for on the only honest ground — a programme he quits is worth nothing.
discussion: Ask which test goes with which component.
Ask the difference between strength and endurance.
Ask why his own earlier score is the right comparison.
Ask what happens to a body trained every day with no rest.
extension: Run the five tests and record them, then repeat them in eight weeks.
Have him design a week's plan that includes two rest days.
misconceptions: "Fit is one thing." It is five, measured five ways.
"More training is always better." Recovery is when it lands.
"Body composition is the real score." It is one of five.
